rationale: The model strongly favors <END> after the final period, despite the observed continuation being a paragraph separator. The existing END-after-punctuation rule is plausible for genuinely finished stories, so this repair preserves it and adds comparable space evidence when a prior paragraph separator is visible and the current context ends in punctuation. This generalizes beyond the observed name and sentence. A prior separator may occur in contexts where a new paragraph is not appropriate, so the rule is provisional and should be checked against replay examples.
